sources.title: Prompting
supporting_claims: Describe the goal, relevant context, expected output, and important boundaries for consequential tasks.
State the result you need while leaving implementation choices to the agent when the route is not itself a requirement.
For Codex tasks, include the relevant code location or reproduction path, constraints, and a way to verify success.
Use focused UI iterations and check the result in the browser.

sources.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
supporting_claims: Store durable repository guidance in AGENTS.md and scope local rules near the code they govern.

sources.title: Best practices for Claude Code
supporting_claims: Give the agent an executable way to verify its work and ask for observable evidence.
Explore before planning and implementing when the task is complex or unfamiliar.
Point to relevant files, existing patterns, or comparable implementations instead of making the agent rediscover repository context.
Correct course early and reset a stuck context after repeated failed corrections.
Use separate context for high-output investigation and independent review.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project
supporting_claims: Keep project instructions concise, specific, consistent, and scoped to where they apply.

sources.title: Create custom subagents
supporting_claims: Give each subagent a specialized purpose and focused responsibility.

sources.title: Reflecting on a year of Claude Code
supporting_claims: Avoid preloading irrelevant context; let the agent retrieve what it needs.
Persist recurring corrections as durable project instructions rather than repeating them in every session.

sources.title: How to build your own AI developer tools with Claude Code
supporting_claims: Use visual specifications for interface-heavy work and give independent reviewers a specific review target.

sources.title: From journalist to iOS developer: How LinkedIn's editor builds with Claude Code
supporting_claims: Separate building from reviewing and isolate AI work in branches or worktrees so experiments remain inspectable and reversible.

sources.title: How Braintrust uses AI agents, evals, and CI to ship better software
supporting_claims: Encode recurring quality expectations as repeatable tests, rubrics, or evals instead of relying on vague requests.

sources.title: How I run autonomous coding agents from my phone with OpenAI Symphony + Linear
supporting_claims: Manage parallel agents with explicit task state, ownership, completion conditions, and a next step after failure.
Audit accumulated instructions and remove context that no longer helps.

sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
supporting_claims: Repeated agent failures often expose a missing tool, abstraction, documentation layer, or enforceable constraint in the environment.
Agent-readable UI state, logs, metrics, and traces shorten runtime debugging loops.
A concise AGENTS.md can act as a map to versioned repository knowledge, while stable architecture rules belong in executable checks.

sources.title: Code review
supporting_claims: Codex can review a specified diff in a read-only pass and return prioritized, actionable findings without changing the worktree.

sources.title: Rules
supporting_claims: Codex rules can narrowly allow, prompt for, or forbid command prefixes and can include positive and negative match tests.

sources.title: Codex GitHub Action
supporting_claims: Stable review and release prompts can be versioned in a repository and run in CI with least GitHub permissions.

sources.title: Build skills
supporting_claims: Stable repeated workflows can be packaged as reusable Skills whose full instructions load only when the task matches.

sources.title: Agent approvals and security
supporting_claims: Dependency setup and credential use should be separated from the agent execution phase so execution can run without secrets and with restricted network access.

sources.title: Automate workflows with hooks
supporting_claims: Deterministic formatting, linting, notifications, and protected-file checks can run at lifecycle hooks instead of depending on repeated prose reminders.

sources.title: Permissions
supporting_claims: Permission rules evaluate deny before ask and allow, enabling protected operations to be blocked before execution.

sources.title: Security
supporting_claims: Third-party MCP servers are not reviewed by Anthropic and should be treated as external dependencies that require explicit trust.

sources.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
supporting_claims: Project MCP servers require approval, tool permissions can be scoped, and unused OAuth authorization can be revoked.

sources.title: Manage costs effectively
supporting_claims: Large tool outputs such as build logs can be filtered to errors and nearby context before entering the conversation.
Code intelligence can reduce repeated broad searches by navigating definitions, references, and type errors directly.

sources.title: Coding sessions
supporting_claims: Agent-ready issues benefit from a clear outcome, scope, constraints, and an example that distinguishes correct behavior from the bug.

sources.title: How we use Linear Agent at Linear
supporting_claims: Cross-system investigations become more tractable when divided into targeted evidence-gathering steps that narrow the next search.

sources.title: Agentic Coding: The Future of Software Development with Agents
supporting_claims: Agent-facing environments work better when logs share one tail-able entry point and tools return specific recoverable errors.

sources.title: Agentic Engineering Patterns: Anti-patterns
supporting_claims: The author of an agent-generated change remains responsible for reviewing it, validating it, keeping the change reviewable, and attaching evidence.
